record_type_quote: This study aims to (1) replicate Jarmolowicz and Lattal’s (2014) procedure with rats and (2) compare resurgence when delays are introduced without altering reinforcement frequency, isolating the effects of delay from rate changes to clarify conditions for resurgence and refine understanding of how degraded reinforcement contributes to behavioral relapse.

targets.authors: Jarmolowicz, D. P., & Lattal, K. A.
targets.title: Resurgence under delayed reinforcement.
targets.evidence_quote: This study aims to (1) replicate Jarmolowicz and Lattal’s (2014) procedure with rats and (2) compare resurgence when delays are introduced without altering reinforcement frequency, isolating the effects of delay from rate changes to clarify conditions for resurgence and refine understanding of how degraded reinforcement contributes to behavioral relapse.
targets.outcome_quote: Our results replicated the findings of Jarmolowicz and Lattal (2014) on delayed alternative reinforcement, originally demonstrated with pigeons.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly state that the replication reproduced the original findings. The added delay-only condition challenges their causal interpretation, without invalidating the test or overturning the stated replication verdict.

reasoning: New rat data explicitly re-test the published pigeon finding. Other resurgence papers are background comparisons, not independently designated targets.
